title: Documents Study Guide
text:
This resource is meant to help you read through the various documents in the Correctional Facility Master Plan Final Report. It is not prepared by legal scholars or subject matter experts. It is a volunteer-led effort. Use it alongside your own critical analysis as an aid, not a thorough summary.
We recommend that you use this guide as a primer before you sit down and read the section of the report you plan to study.

title: Documents Study Guide
text:
Commentary
Beyond the summary above, there are a number of points of interest in this MOA. First, the County is only making incremental changes, and the process of reforming the jails remains an ongoing process (eg. the unresolved issues and the suspension of the IHSF plan). There are at least a few major factors that appear to have led to this protracted reform as indicated implicitly or explicitly in this MOA: maintaining current priorities (eg. the status quo levels of incarceration, give or take some inmate capacity); compliance with the Mays Consent Decree; compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA); and anticipating future needs of incarceration (eg. how much capacity will be needed).
The monitoring report of the “Subject Matter Expert” (SME) mentioned in this MOA is worth exploring as it provides the documented issues of the jails in a manner that has to be recognized and acknowledged by the County given its legal weight as a component of the MCD settlement. Perhaps what is most striking is the excerpt taken from the report in which the SME states, “The County must take immediate steps to secure appropriate inpatient mental health treatment and a continuum of services for people in their custody with serious mental health needs” (4). The emphasis on urgency is notable given that the final report appears to delay the completion of necessary changes to mental health services far into the future given the proposed timeline for completing facility development.2
Among the stated requirements for the Correctional Facility Master Plan is a list of mental health care objectives as stipulated by the Mays Consent Decree (6). These agreed upon steps are meant to provide:

programming
capacity
space
staffing

In other words, if the CFMP does not satisfy the MCD, it may not be approved.
As mentioned above, the final section of the MOA “recognizes” that a population reduction of the jails would help with compliance with the MCD. It lists a few options that could be considered in the CFMP to facilitate this reduction:

diversion
out-of-custody mental health treatment settings
substance use
and other programs as alternatives to incarceration (9).
